answer: Require each identity to commit a fingerprint of the model actually doing its work — hashed weights plus a behavioral trace no copy can hide. Clones running one shared model light up as a single ferrous core under the prism of comparison: identical fingerprints cluster, and the cluster splits one capped weight. A trellis of distinct models is expensive to grow, since each clone needs real retraining, not a keypair. Limits: open-weight models share fingerprints legitimately, so the check must weigh behavior, not just weights.
